\x3C/ul>\x3C/div>\x3C/figure>\x3Cp>\x3C/p>\x3Cp style=\"text-align: left;\">Right triangles \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper P upper Q upper R\">\x3Cmrow> \x3Cmi>P\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>Q\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>R\x3C/mi> \x3C/mrow> \x3C/math> and \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper S upper T upper U\">\x3Cmrow> \x3Cmi>S\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>T\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>U\x3C/mi> \x3C/mrow> \x3C/math> are similar, where \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper If the measure of angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper Q\">\x3Cmi>Q\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> is \x3Cmath alttext=\"18 degree\">\x3Cmrow>\x3Cmn>18\x3C/mn>\x3C/mrow>\x3Cmo>&#176;\x3C/mo>\x3C/math>, what is the measure of angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper S\">\x3Cmi>S\x3C/mi> \x3C/math>?\x3C/p>",rationale:"\x3Cp>Choice B is correct. In similar triangles, corresponding angles are congruent. It&rsquo;s given that right triangles \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper P upper Q upper R\">\x3Cmrow> \x3Cmi>P\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>Q\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>R\x3C/mi> \x3C/mrow> \x3C/math> and \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper S upper T upper U\">\x3Cmrow> \x3Cmi>S\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>T\x3C/mi> \x3Cmi>U\x3C/mi> \x3C/mrow> \x3C/math> are similar, where angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper P\">\x3Cmi>P\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> corresponds to angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper S\">\x3Cmi>S\x3C/mi> \x3C/math>. It follows that angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper P\">\x3Cmi>P\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> is congruent to angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper S\">\x3Cmi>S\x3C/mi> \x3C/math>. In the triangles shown, angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper R\">\x3Cmi>R\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> and angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper U\">\x3Cmi>U\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> are both marked as right angles, so angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper R\">\x3Cmi>R\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> and angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper U\">\x3Cmi>U\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> are corresponding angles. It follows that angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper Q\">\x3Cmi>Q\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> and angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper T\">\x3Cmi>T\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> are corresponding angles, and thus, angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper Q\">\x3Cmi>Q\x3C/mi> \x3C/math> is congruent to angle \x3Cmath alttext=\"upper T\">\x3Cmi>T\x3C/mi> \x3C/math>. The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a triangle is \x3Cmath alttext=\"180 degree\">\x3Cmn>180\x3C/mn>\x3Cmo>°\x3C/mo>\x3C/math>.
